item.title: 🎧 LISTEN #1 — Jason & Scot Show: E343 - Amazon Q2 2026 Earnings
item.content:encoded:
Score: 81/100 | Listen Fully | Confidence: low

Originally published 03 Aug 2026

Provides a highly relevant and data-driven strategic analysis of Amazon's Q2 earnings, focusing on critical areas like AWS growth, aggressive AI investments (including custom chips and robotics), and retail performance. The insights are delivered by authoritative eCommerce experts and directly inform product strategy, competitive analysis, and understanding market dynamics at a senior level. (carried over)

Summary

This episode offers a comprehensive breakdown of Amazon's Q2 earnings, with a sharp focus on AWS's sustained growth, improved margins, and Wall Street's reaction to Amazon's substantial AI investments. Hosts Jason Goldberg and Scot Wingo delve into key strategic areas including Amazon's retail performance, gains in everyday essentials, advancements in robotics, the development of custom AI chips like Trainium and Graviton, and the rapid expansion of the company's advertising business. The discussion also touches on broader trends such as how social media, micro-influencers, and AI-powered shopping agents are transforming consumer travel discovery. This analysis provides critical insights into the strategic direction and financial health of a major player in eCommerce and technology.

Key Ideas

  • Amazon's aggressive AI investments, including custom chips (Trainium, Graviton) and robotics, driving AWS growth and strategic direction.
  • Detailed analysis of Amazon's Q2 earnings, covering retail performance, advertising business expansion, and market reactions.
  • The evolving landscape of consumer discovery and booking, influenced by AI-powered shopping agents and micro-influencers.

item.title: 🎧 LISTEN #2 — Jason & Scot Show: EP342 - The End of the Attention Economy, and What Retail Does Next with Mitch Joel
item.content:encoded:
Score: 75/100 | Listen Fully | Confidence: low

Originally published 31 Jul 2026

Explores a compelling strategic thesis on the 'intimacy economy' and its profound implications for retail and AI-driven customer experiences. The discussion covers critical topics like AI's role in curation, agentic shopping, and internal vs. customer-facing AI deployment, offering forward-looking insights highly relevant for product strategy and craft at a senior level. (carried over)

Summary

Recorded live from NRF Nexus, this episode features a discussion with keynote speaker Mitch Joel, who posits that the 'attention economy' is over, giving way to an 'intimacy economy' where brands must deliver highly personalized customer experiences. The conversation explores how digital commerce has disrupted serendipity and discovery, and how AI can scale curation to become a competitive advantage. It delves into the practicalities of agentic shopping, whether consumers truly desire it, and the current deployment of AI in companies, often prioritizing internal productivity over direct customer interaction. The episode concludes with a nuanced discussion on trust in AI, particularly in scenarios where AI improves experience but disclosure might be counterproductive.

Key Ideas

  • The shift from an 'attention economy' to an 'intimacy economy' in retail, emphasizing hyper-personalized customer experiences.
  • AI's role in restoring serendipity and discovery through scalable curation, and the implications of agentic shopping.
  • Strategic considerations for AI deployment in companies, balancing internal productivity with customer-facing applications and the challenge of trust.
